title: A free, hand-built haunted castle in Mass. is drawing huge Halloween crowds
excerpt: Nightmare on Moore Street is back for its fourth year, featuring its most extravagant display to date.
content:
An East Boston home is celebrating Halloween with its most extravagant display to date, garnering thousands of spectators and viral fame in the process.

Nightmare on Moore Street is back at 35 Moore St. for its fourth year, with newlywed Jimmy Magnasco and his family turning the house into a free Halloween display.

The castle-inspired design was unveiled on Oct. 20 and quickly went viral on TikTok and Instagram, racking up hundreds of thousands of views to date.

This year's display features several devilish animatronic characters, an eerie horse-riding skeleton and a giant jack-o-lantern with shifting expressions.

Almost the entire set was hand-built by Magnasco, who bought materials from Home Depot.

"It was a lot of work," Magnasco told local content creator Marc Lewis, adding that it took "months and months of planning" to paint, carve and build the setup.

The homeowner said more pieces will be added to the display, leading up to Halloween. On that night, the building will turn into a walk-through haunted house with live actors.

Before his display went viral, Magnasco said he was expecting roughly 2,000 people to come check out the spine-tingling house. He now expects a larger crowd this Halloween.

"I feel like everyone has so much fun," Magnasco told Lewis.

A house in East Boston has gone viral for its extravagant Halloween display, which has been dubbed "Nightmare on Moore Street."David Cifarelli

Nightmare on Moore Street's display has varied over the years, starting with an extraterrestrial theme in 2023. Last year's setup featured some similar elements, including the giant jack-o-lantern, but this is the first year that Magnasco completely transformed his home's exterior.

Nightmare on Moore Street is open from 5 to 11 p.m. nightly. Street parking is tight, so people are encouraged to take the Blue Line to Wood Island and walk over. People can support Nightmare on Moore Street by making a donation.
